page.notes: Long s rendered as plain s per the rules; the page as printed uses long s throughout, so the transcription above normalises it to s. Fragment "ca os." at the foot continues from the last line and is kept as a fragment. Line-end hyphens: "appe-rit" (appe-rit), "ena-sci" and similar are joined only where the printed hyphen is visible. Possible misreadings: "Blattę" (Blatte or Blattę), "ꝑ" at the start of the line "materiæ" (printed as a p-with-stroke), "nitrum" is read as printed; "cura" in "curā" has a macron as printed. Line "cum ardente rubore, duri, & cū" is read as printed; the ampersand near "duri" is a clear &. Right-edge cut-off words on several lines are partly lost to the page edge and are marked as read.
